info.title: FPChecker API
info.summary: The customer-facing HTTP API of FPChecker.
info.description:
Identify a device, decide whether it may claim or use something, and read what was seen.
Hand-written from the route handlers; `worker/test/openapi-contract.test.ts` checks it against the running
server (the route set, the examples and the real answers).

**Keys.** A project has a secret key (`sk_…`, header `X-Secret-Key`, backend only) and a publishable key
(`pk_…`, header `X-Publishable-Key`, safe in a browser or app). `/v2/challenge` and `/v2/identify` take the
publishable key; every other keyed route takes the secret key. The wrong kind of key is `401`.

**Errors.** Most failures are `{ "ok": false, "error": "<code>" }` (`Error`). Routes that make a decision
or record something answer in their own shape: `{ "ok": false, "reason": "<code>" }` plus the fields the
route normally has (`EligibilityRefusal`, `QuotaRefusal`, `ReleaseRefusal`, `SubjectRefusal`,
`FeedbackRefusal`, `IdentifyRefusal`, `ReasonError`). Some failures are deliberately HTTP 200 with
`ok: false` (a fail-closed internal error, `maintenance`, most identify refusals): **test `ok`, not only the
status**. Never treat a response without `ok: true` as a success.

**Billing.** On a metered project a billed call with an empty balance is `402 { "ok": false, "error":
"insufficient_credits" }`, and `503 commit_uncertain` means the charge may have happened. A billed call is
never safe to retry blindly.

**Forward compatibility.** Clients must tolerate unknown enum values in response fields (for example `reason`,
`error` and signal kinds) and unknown object properties. New values and properties may be added without a
version bump; treat an unrecognised value as a generic refusal or ignore it, never as a parse failure.

**Management API.** Routes under `/v1/management/` take a management key (`mk_…`, header
`Authorization: Bearer`) instead of a project key, and act on the whole account: its projects, environments,
webhooks, rulesets, usage and audit log. Keys have a `read` or a `write` scope. Answers are
`{ "ok": true, … }` or `{ "ok": false, "error": "<code>" }`. Each account may make 120 reads and 30 changes
per minute. Billing, members, management keys, signing keys, proxy secrets and domains are not on this plane.

**Not in this file.** Admin, console and network-check routes, and the older v1 challenge and identify
protocol, are not part of the customer contract. The production API serves no OpenAPI route of its own.

tags.name: Identify
tags.description: Browser and app side (publishable key), plus the backend call that starts it.

tags.name: Decisions
tags.description: Backend calls that spend an attestation (secret key).

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Read and annotate what identify recorded (secret key).

tags.name: Bots
tags.description: Header-only bot check for requests your backend received (secret key).

tags.name: Management
tags.description: Manage the account's projects, environments, webhooks and rulesets from your own tooling (management key). Separate from the project keys above.

post.summary: Create an intent for the next identify
post.description:
Your backend names what the next identify is for. The returned `intentToken` goes to your client, which
passes it to `GET /v2/challenge` and `POST /v2/identify`. Stateless and free. Treat the token as opaque.
A fail-closed server error is `200 { "ok": false, "error": "temporarily_unavailable" }`.

200.description: The intent, or a fail-closed refusal (check `ok`).

get.summary: Get a challenge for an intent
get.description:
Called by the client (publishable key). The `intent` must be URL-encoded. An intent can fetch several
challenges until it expires (for example a second identify after a proof-of-work request).

parameters.name: intent
parameters.description: The `intentToken` your backend created.

parameters.name: difficulty
parameters.description: Ask for a proof-of-work challenge of this many zero bits (8 to 28).

200.description: The challenge, or a fail-closed refusal (check `ok`).

403.description: `project_disabled`, or `request_filtered` when the project's request filters (allowed origins, IP deny list, header rules, crawler blocking) refuse the request. A filtered request is not billed and records no event.

post.description:
Called by the client (publishable key) with the components it collected. The answer carries one opaque
`attestation` for your backend to spend, the `eventId` of the recorded event and, when the project has
sealed results enabled, a `sealedResult` your backend decrypts with the project's sealing key.

Refusals are mostly HTTP 200 with `ok: false` and a `reason` (`IdentifyRefusal`); a rate limit or the
daily identify cap is 429, no credits is 402. **A success without a non-empty string `attestation` is a
failure.**

sealed.summary: Web identify of a project with sealed results on

403.description: `project_disabled`, or `request_filtered` when the project's request filters (allowed origins, IP deny list, header rules, crawler blocking) refuse the request. A filtered request is not billed and records no event.

429.description: Rate limited, or `identify_daily_limit` on a metered account.

post.summary: Decide whether this device may claim, and optionally record the claim
post.description:
Backend only. Spends the attestation from identify. With `claim: true` an `allow` records one claim
atomically and the answer carries its `claimId`. Business outcomes (deny, turnstile, pow) are HTTP 200
with `ok: true` and an `action`: grant only on `eligible === true`. Billed; never retried automatically.
Pass the real end-user IP as `clientIp`.

**Attestation refusals.** Only a missing or non-object `attestation` is HTTP 400. An expired or altered
attestation, one issued for another purpose, or one whose subject differs is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`
and `reason` `bad_attestation`, `attestation_purpose`, `attestation_subject` or (when the project requires
intents) `intent_required`: **test `ok`, not only the status**.

200.description: The decision (check `eligible` and `action`), or a fail-closed refusal.

400.description: `bad_attestation`: the `attestation` is missing or not an object.

post.description:
Backend only. Idempotent: releasing a released claim answers `released: true` with
`already_released`. A refusal to release is HTTP 200 with `ok: true` and `released: false`.

200.description: The outcome (check `released`), or a fail-closed refusal.

post.summary: Check or consume a windowed usage quota, or give a use back
post.description:
Backend only. Same envelope as eligibility, without an email. Without `consume` it is a read-only probe;
with `consume` an `allow` records one use (an `idempotencyKey` makes a retry count once). With
`release: true` and the `idempotencyKey` it gives that use back and needs no attestation. A quota name
the project has not configured is denied, never unlimited. Billed; never retried automatically.

**Attestation refusals.** Only a missing or non-object `attestation` is HTTP 400. An expired or altered
attestation, one issued for another purpose, or one whose subject differs is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`
and `reason` `bad_attestation`, `attestation_purpose`, `attestation_subject` or (when the project requires
intents) `intent_required`: **test `ok`, not only the status**.

200.description: The decision (check `allowed` and `action`), the release outcome, or a fail-closed refusal.

400.description: `bad_attestation` (the `attestation` is missing or not an object) or `bad_request`.

post.summary: Bind a subject (for example an inviter) to the attested device
post.description:
Backend only. The attestation must come from an intent created for purpose `subjects` with the same
`subject`. Billed; never retried automatically.

**Attestation refusals.** Only a missing or non-object `attestation` is HTTP 400. An expired or altered
attestation, one issued for another purpose, or one whose subject differs is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`
and `reason` `bad_attestation`, `attestation_purpose`, `attestation_subject` or (when the project requires
intents) `intent_required`: **test `ok`, not only the status**.

400.description: `bad_request`, `bad_subject`, or `bad_attestation` (the `attestation` is missing or not an object).

post.summary: Compare the attested device with a subject's bound devices
post.description:
Backend only. Read only; `suggestion` is advice, the decision is yours. A refusal carries
`suggestion: review` so a caller that reads only the suggestion never sees an allow from a check that did
not run. Billed; never retried automatically.

**Attestation refusals.** Only a missing or non-object `attestation` is HTTP 400. An expired or altered
attestation, one issued for another purpose, or one whose subject differs is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`
and `reason` `bad_attestation`, `attestation_purpose`, `attestation_subject` or (when the project requires
intents) `intent_required`: **test `ok`, not only the status**.

200.description: The comparison, or a fail-closed refusal (check `ok`).

400.description: `bad_request`, `bad_subject`, or `bad_attestation` (the `attestation` is missing or not an object).

post.summary: Say what a visitor or claim turned out to be
post.description:
Backend only. Labels are input for offline analysis and never change a live decision. Exactly one of
`visitorId` and `claimId`. Not charged on metered projects (a zero balance still answers 402).

200.description: Recorded, or a fail-closed refusal (`recorded` is false).

400.description: `bad_request`: both or neither id, a bad `label` or `reason`, or a malformed id.

404.description: The claim is not this project's, or the visitor was not seen in the last 90 days.

get.summary: List claims later found to share a household
get.description:
Backend only. Oldest first. `next` is the cursor for the following page (pass it as `after`). It is
`null` on the last page, but also non-null when a page is exactly full, so the page after it can be empty:
loop until `next` is null.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `flagId` to continue after. Default `0`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 500. Default 100.

500.description: Fail-closed server error (never an empty page).

post.summary: Check a request your backend received
post.description:
Backend only. Forward the method, URL, client address and headers of a request you received and get back
who or what sent it. Header-only: no script ran in the sender, so `bot.types` holds only the types the
headers give away (`automation_tool`, `headless`, `missing_headers`). The address facts (`ip`, `vpn`,
`proxy`) come from our own data; there is no device clock, so no `timezone_mismatch`. Not charged, and no
event is written.

`bot.result` is `good` for a verified or signed directory bot, `bad` for a directory bot that is not
(`unknown` or `spoofed`) or for any request whose headers gave it away, and `not_detected` otherwise.
Only signers listed in the Bot directory can be `signed`; a valid signature from anyone else is ignored.

Send `url` as the visitor requested it: the original host and scheme, not the address of your origin behind
a CDN or load balancer. A signed request is checked against that host. Chrome sends no client hints over
plain http, so the missing-client-hints rule only applies to `https` URLs.

Forward only the headers you need, never `Cookie` or `Authorization`: `user-agent`, `accept`,
`accept-language`, `accept-encoding`, `sec-ch-ua`, `sec-ch-ua-mobile`, `sec-ch-ua-platform`,
`sec-fetch-site`, `sec-fetch-mode`, `sec-fetch-dest`, `sec-fetch-user`, `signature`, `signature-input`,
`signature-agent`, `upgrade-insecure-requests`, and every header named in the request's `Signature-Input`
(a covered header you leave out makes the signature uncheckable: the identity is `unknown`). The body is at
most 32 KiB, with at most 64 headers (values up to 4096 characters) and a `url` up to 2048 characters.

`ip` is the client address your platform vouches for, never a value the visitor can set: Express `req.ip`
with a hop-count `trust proxy`; Next.js the header your own proxy sets (for example `x-real-ip`), never the
leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is read as the IPv4 address.

Call it once per visitor request and reuse the answer. Never retry a signed request: the second attempt
replays the nonce and comes back `spoofed`.

Limits: 1200 requests per minute per project (`429` with `reason: rate_limited`) and 3000 per minute per
calling address, checked before authentication (`429` with `error: rate_limited`). Treat both bodies as
rate limited.

headers.user-agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/126.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

get.description:
Newest first, scoped to the caller's project. Any combination of the parameters; an unknown, repeated or
malformed parameter is `400 invalid_request`. The signal filters match the event's `signals`; an event whose
value is `null` matches neither `true` nor `false`.

parameters.name: visitorId
parameters.description: Exact match.

parameters.name: linkedId
parameters.description: Exact match.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: One address, or a CIDR no wider than IPv4 /16 or IPv6 /48.

parameters.name: bot
parameters.description: `true` matches events where the bot result is `bad` (good bots are not counted), `false` those where it is `not_detected`. An event whose bot result is `good` matches neither `true` nor `false`; in a rule the field `bot` is `false` for a good bot.

parameters.name: bot_result
parameters.description: Exact match on `signals.bot.result`. Events stored before server 0.48.0 have no `good`.

parameters.name: bot_category
parameters.description: Exact match on `signals.bot.info.category`; events without a directory match have none.

parameters.name: bot_identity
parameters.description: Exact match on `signals.bot.info.identity`.

parameters.name: bot_id
parameters.description: Exact match on `signals.bot.info.id`, one of the ids in the Bot directory.

parameters.name: incognito
parameters.description: Reserved. Both `true` and `false` match nothing today, because the value is always null (null matches neither).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: ISO 8601 date or time. Default the last 7 days (or the retention, if shorter). The span cannot exceed the project's retention.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: ISO 8601 date or time. Default now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next` of the previous page.

patch.description:
Any of `linkedId`, `tags` and `suspect`; `null` clears `linkedId` and `tags`. An unknown field, an empty
body or an invalid value is `400 invalid_request` and changes nothing.

get.description: `404` for a visitor this project has not seen within its retention.

delete.summary: Erase a visitor for this project
delete.description:
Erases this project's events, queued and past webhook deliveries and device rows for the visitor.
`shared: true` means another project also uses the device, whose rows were kept. A second call is `404`.
If the rate limiter itself fails the call refuses with `503 unavailable` and deletes nothing: retry it.

503.description: The rate limiter is unavailable; nothing was deleted.

get.description: Proves the process answers; it stays green with the database or cache down. Use `/status` for that.

get.summary: Can the API serve identify and claims right now
get.description: Booleans only, cached for 15 seconds. `503` with the same body when a dependency is down or the server is in maintenance.
Status, credit balance and the most recent credit lots (up to 200, newest first). Needs the `read` scope.
Billed calls per day, project and endpoint. At most 92 days per request; the default is the last 30 days. Needs the `read` scope.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC). Default 29 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC). Default today.

get.description:
Every change made to the account through the console or the Management API, newest first. Entries are kept
for 400 days. Page with `nextCursor`. Needs the `read` scope.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Exact action name, for example `project.update`.

parameters.name: actorId
parameters.description: Exact actor id (a user id, or a management key id such as `mkey_0123456789ab`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound, ISO 8601 date or date-time.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound, ISO 8601 date or date-time.

get.description: The account's projects, environments included, oldest first. Needs the `read` scope.

post.description: The new project's `secretKey` and `publishableKey` are in this answer and nowhere else. Needs the `write` scope.

patch.description:
Any of the listed fields; an empty body is `400 nothing_to_update`. Setting `disabled` to `false` on an
environment counts against the limit of three enabled environments (`409 environment_limit`).
A body containing `claimGroupId` is refused with `400 invalid_field`: claim groups are console-only.
Needs the `write` scope.

delete.description:
Only a project that was never used can be deleted; otherwise `409 project_in_use` (disable it instead).
A project that still has environments is `409 environments_remaining`. Needs the `write` scope.

post.description: Replaces the project's secret or publishable key. The old key stops working at once; the new one is in this answer and nowhere else. Needs the `write` scope.

An environment is a project of its own under a top-level project, with its own keys and events. It starts
with a copy of the parent's settings (policy, allowed origins, request filters, ruleset, event retention, and
the native and human-check credentials); webhooks, signing keys, proxy secrets, domains and claim groups are
not copied. At most three enabled environments per project (ten in total, disabled ones included).
`skipped` lists settings that could not be copied. Needs the `write` scope.

201.description: Created. The new keys are in this answer and nowhere else.

post.description:
Overwrites this project's settings with those of another project of the same family (the parent or a sibling
environment). `404 project_not_found` for anything that is not in the same family. Needs the `write` scope.

200.description: The endpoints. Secrets are never listed.

post.description:
The URL must be `https` and resolve to a public address. The signing `secret` is in this answer and nowhere
else. A project has a limited number of endpoints (`409 limit_reached`). Needs the `write` scope.

patch.summary: Enable or disable a webhook endpoint

post.description: The new `secret` is in this answer and nowhere else. Needs the `write` scope.

200.description: The stored ruleset (`version` 0 when none was ever saved).

put.description:
Replaces the whole ruleset. `ifVersion` is the `version` this edit was based on; if the stored version has
moved the answer is `409 version_conflict` with the current `version`, and nothing is saved. A rejected
ruleset is `400 invalid_ruleset` with the `path` of the first problem. Needs the `write` scope.

200.description: The saved ruleset, one version higher.

post.description:
Evaluates a draft against one stored event and saves nothing. It changes nothing, so it needs only the `read`
scope, counts against the read rate limit, and still works while the account is under review.

200.description: What the draft would decide for that event.

get.description:
The same filters, paging and limits as `searchEvents` (`GET /v1/events`), for the project in the path.
Needs the `read` scope.

parameters.name: bot
parameters.description: `true` matches events where the bot result is `bad` (good bots are not counted), `false` those where it is `not_detected`. An event whose bot result is `good` matches neither `true` nor `false`.

get.description: Erasing a visitor is not available here. Needs the `read` scope.

post.summary: A new event, sent to your endpoint
post.description:
Sent to each HTTPS endpoint you register in the console, once per recorded event (at least once: ignore a
repeated `FPC-Delivery-Id` or `eventId`). Answer any `2xx` within 3 seconds. A failed delivery is retried up
to 6 times in total.

Verify `FPC-Signature` before trusting the body: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` (hex in either case) where `v1` is the
HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the endpoint secret (the whole `whsec_…` string), of `<t>.<raw request body>`.
Use the raw bytes you received, never re-serialised JSON; compare in constant time; reject a `t` more than
300 seconds from your clock. The header may carry more than one `v1`; any valid one passes.

parameters.name: FPC-Delivery-Id
parameters.description: `whd_…`, the same on every retry of this delivery.

secretKey.name: X-Secret-Key
secretKey.description: The project's secret key (`sk_…`). Backend only.

publishableKey.name: X-Publishable-Key
publishableKey.description: The project's publishable key (`pk_…`). Safe in a browser or app.

managementKey.description:
A management key, format `mk_…` (`mk_` plus 43 URL-safe characters), sent as `Authorization: Bearer mk_…`.
Created and revoked in the console, shown once. Scope `read` allows `GET` routes and the ruleset dry run;
scope `write` allows everything on this plane. Any key that is unknown, revoked, expired, malformed or
belongs to a deleted account is the same `401 invalid_management_key`.

ManagementUnauthorized.description: The management key is missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired. One answer for all of them.

ManagementInsufficientScope.description: The key has the `read` scope and this route needs `write`.

ManagementAccountReview.description: The account is under review. Reads and the ruleset dry run still work; changes are refused.

ManagementRateLimited.description: The account's budget is spent (120 reads or 30 changes per minute, counted separately). Nothing was changed; retry after `Retry-After` seconds (the counters are fixed 60-second windows). If the limiter itself cannot be reached the call is refused the same way.

ManagementNotFound.description: The project, webhook, event or visitor does not exist, or is not this account's. All of those answer the same, so ids cannot be probed. A path the Management API does not have is also `404 not_found`.

ManagementInvalid.description: A malformed parameter or body. `error` names the problem (`invalid_name`, `invalid_body`, `invalid_ruleset`, ...); `invalid_ruleset` and `invalid_request_filters` add a `path`.

ManagementConflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state (`environment_limit`, `environment_exists`, `not_top_level`, `environments_remaining`, `project_in_use`, `version_conflict`, `limit_reached`).

ManagementCommitUncertain.description: The database did not confirm whether this change was committed. Read the resource to see whether it took effect before repeating the call.

ManagementUncertainOrUnavailable.description: Either a limiter this route depends on could not be reached and nothing was changed (`unavailable`; retry), or the database did not confirm whether the change was committed (`commit_uncertain`; read the resource before repeating).

ManagementUnavailable.description: A limiter this route depends on could not be reached; nothing was changed. Retry.

Unauthorized.description: The key is missing, malformed, unknown, or of the wrong kind for this route.

InsufficientCredits.description: A metered project with an empty balance.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests from this address (the answer may also come before authentication).

RateLimitedReason.description: Rate limited, by the route's own limit (body `{ ok: false, reason: rate_limited }`) or by the per-IP limit that runs before authentication (body `{ ok: false, error: rate_limited }`). Clients must accept both bodies.

CommitUncertain.description: The database did not confirm whether the decision and its charge were committed. The call may have been charged; it is not replayed automatically.

InvalidRequest.description: An unknown, repeated or malformed parameter or body field.

NotFound.description: Malformed, missing, or another project's id: all answer the same, so ids cannot be probed.

InternalError.description: Fail-closed server error (never an empty result).

status.description: `active`, or `review` while the account is under review. New values may be added.

type.description: `user`, `management_key` or `system`. New values may be added.

action.description: A dotted name such as `project.update`. New actions may be added.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor`; null on the last page.

sealKey.description: Read-only here. The browser agent's upload key; it ships in the customer's page. Managed in the console.

hasTurnstileSecret.description: The secret itself is never returned.

nativeConfig.description: App credentials with all key material left out.

policy.description: The project's policy settings. New settings may be added.

claimGroupId.description: Read-only here; set in the console. A PATCH containing it is refused with `invalid_field`.

requestFilters.description: Request filters: `ipDeny`, `headerRules`, `blockCrawlers`. `blockCrawlers` refuses every directory bot by User-Agent, including search engines and synthetic monitors (Datadog Synthetics, Checkly, UptimeRobot, Lighthouse, GTmetrix); to allow some of them use rules (an allow rule on `botId`) with the filter off, since the filter runs before rules.

environment.description: `production` for a top-level project, otherwise the environment name.

environmentOf.description: The parent project's id; null for a top-level project.

ManagementProjectPatch.description: At least one field. Unlisted fields are ignored.

policy.description: The settings to change; the rest keep their values.

key.description: The new key (`sk_…` or `pk_…`). Shown once.

name.description: Lower case; `production` is the top-level project and cannot be used.

skipped.description: Settings that could not be copied and were left empty. New values may be added.

from.description: Another project of the same family.

secret.description: The new signing secret. Shown once.

id.description: Keeps the id of an existing rule; omit for a new one.

ifVersion.description: The `version` this edit is based on.

type.description: `allow`, `human_check`, `deny`, or `none` when no rule matched. New values may be added.

next.description: Pass as `cursor`. Can be non-null on an exactly full last page: loop until it is null.

Error.description: The common failure shape. `error` is a stable code.

RateLimitError.description: The per-IP limit that runs before authentication answers this on every route, whatever shape the route's own errors have.

ReasonError.description: A failure that names its code in `reason`.

maintenance.description: Present only while the server is in maintenance.

purpose.description: `claim:<kind>` (kind `trial` unless the project configures others), `quota:<name>` or `subjects`.

subject.description: Optional, 1 to 200 characters, no control characters. When set, the decision call must pass the same `subject`.

clientIp.description: The end user's IP, for rate limiting. Take it only from your own edge.

NativeProof.description: A platform proof, bound to the request by the SDK.

pow.description: Proof-of-work solution, when the challenge asked for one.

linkedId.description: Your own id for this visit (1 to 256 characters, no control characters). Not covered by any platform proof.

tags.description: A JSON object of at most 4096 bytes, nested at most 3 levels. Not covered by any platform proof.

attestation.description: Opaque. Send it unchanged to your backend.

proofStatus.description: Native platforms only. `unknown_key` means re-attest the App Attest key and retry once.

sealedResult.description:
Present only when the project has an active sealing key, and never on a refusal. Standard base64 (with
padding) of `"fps1" | keyId(4) | nonce(12) | AES-256-GCM ciphertext and 16-byte tag`; keyId is the first
4 bytes of SHA-256(key) and the first 8 bytes are the AAD. Decrypt it in your backend with the project's
sealing key (keep the previous key too during a rotation). The plaintext is identity-only JSON:
`version` (1), `eventId`, `visitorId`, `projectId`, `linkedId` (or null), `tags` (or null), `timestamp`
(Unix ms), `platform` and `proofStatus` (always `none` on web). There is no IP address, no signals, no
score and no decision in it. Full format and a sample: docs/INTEGRATION.md, "Sealed results".

A sealed result is proof of origin, not a grant: it shows FPChecker produced this event for a project,
nothing more. It does not expire and anyone who holds the blob can replay it. Before you trust one,
check that `projectId` is yours, reject a `timestamp` older than a short window (5 minutes is a good
default; make it configurable), and treat `eventId` as single-use or require `linkedId` to match the
current session or user. Never grant a trial, coupon or credit from it: use `POST /v1/eligibility`
with the attestation for that.

IdentifyResponse.description:
Projects whose administrator enabled score details also get `visitorId`, `trustScore`, `identityConfidence`,
`isNew` and rule diagnostics here. Do not branch on them.

subject.description: Must equal the intent's subject when the intent named one.

claim.description: Record one claim when the decision is allow.

idempotent.description: With `claim`, answer allow again (`replayed: true`) when the same identity claimed within 24 hours.

reason.description: See "Handle the result" in docs/INTEGRATION.md. Includes `rule_deny` (a deny rule matched; `ruleId` says which) and `rule_allow` (an allow rule let a first claim through the first-claim and trust gates; in a shared device class it skips only the datacenter check and the human check still runs). New values may be added; treat an unknown value as a generic refusal.

powDifficulty.description: With action `pow` (or `turnstile` in `either` mode), the zero bits a proof needs.

Signals.description:
What the server learned about the visit. **Unknown is `null`, never `false`**: `false` means the check ran
and found nothing. Evidence to weigh, not verdicts. `version` is `2` for every event stored by server
0.48.0 or later; older events are read back as version 1 (no `good` result and no `bot.info`).

SignalsV1.description: Signals of an event stored before server 0.48.0.

SignalsV2.description: Signals of an event stored by server 0.48.0 or later.

result.description: `good` is a directory bot whose identity is `verified` or `signed`. A directory bot that is `unknown` or `spoofed` is `bad`. New values may be added; treat an unknown value as `bad`.

info.description: Who the bot is, when the request named an entry of the Bot directory; otherwise `null`.

BotType.description: New values may be added; ignore a value you do not know.

BotHeaderType.description: What the headers of a single request give away. New values may be added; ignore a value you do not know.

BotCategory.description: New values may be added; treat an unknown value as `other`.

BotIdentity.description: `verified` = the address matches the operator's published ranges or reverse DNS; `signed` = a valid signature from a signer listed in the Bot directory; `unknown` = could not be confirmed; `spoofed` = claims to be the bot, but the address or signature says otherwise.

BotId.description: The id of an entry of the Bot directory. New ids are added as the directory grows.

BotInfo.description: One entry of the Bot directory and how well the request matched it.

id.description: Stable id, for example `googlebot`; the values of `bot_id`.

url.description: An absolute http or https URL, as the visitor requested it (original host and scheme).

ip.description: The client address of the request (IPv4 or IPv6

headers.description: The request headers listed in the operation description, never `Cookie` or `Authorization`. Names are case-insensitive.

asName.description: Where you show it, add "IP address data powered by IPinfo".

items.description: New values may be added; ignore a value you do not know.

type.description: `none` when the ruleset was evaluated and no rule matched. New values may be added; treat an unknown value as `none`.

ruleId.description: The matching rule; absent when `type` is `none`.

suspect.description: Yours to set with `updateEvent`; always false in a webhook.

proxied.description: True when the request reached the API through the project's Cloudflare proxy integration with a valid proxy secret.

ruleAction.description: What the project's ruleset decided for this event. Null when the ruleset is disabled. Never in the browser or app identify answer or a sealed result.

Event.description: An event as the read API returns it (`signals` is always present, `null` when the event has none).

WebhookEvent.description:
The event JSON as a webhook body. `signals` can be missing from a payload queued before server 0.43.0
(treat missing and `null` alike); `proxied` and `ruleAction` can be missing from a payload queued before server 0.45.0. A console "Test" delivery adds `"test": true`.

next.description: Pass as `cursor`. Can be non-null on an exactly full last page, so the next page may be empty: loop until it is null.

shared.description: True when another project also uses the device; its rows were kept.
